title: Advanced Navigation and Deep Linking
description: Learn how to implement advanced navigation patterns in React Native apps and enable deep linking to navigate directly to specific screens.

lessons.title: Recap: React Navigation Basics
lessons.content: React Navigation is the most popular library for navigation in React Native. It supports stack, tab, and drawer navigators. You create a navigator and add screens to it, enabling navigation between screens.

lessons.title: Nested Navigators
lessons.content: Nested navigators allow you to combine multiple navigation types. For example, you can have a tab navigator where each tab contains its own stack navigator, allowing complex navigation flows.

lessons.title: Example: Creating Nested Navigators
Passing Params Between Screens
What is Deep Linking?
lessons.content: Deep linking lets your app respond to URLs, so users can open specific screens directly from a link, outside the app. Useful for sharing content, notifications, or marketing.

lessons.title: Setting Up Deep Linking in React Navigation
Handling Incoming Links
lessons.content: When the app opens from a link, React Navigation parses the URL and navigates to the matching screen, passing URL parameters as screen params automatically.

lessons.title: Example: Deep Linking URL to Screen
Testing Deep Linking
lessons.content: Test deep linking on iOS and Android simulators or devices by opening URLs manually using commands like `xcrun simctl openurl` (iOS) or `adb shell am start` (Android).

lessons.title: Best Practices for Navigation and Deep Linking
lessons.content:
- Keep URLs simple and predictable
- Handle missing or invalid params gracefully
- Combine deep linking with authentication flows
- Document your URL scheme for users and marketing
